ADDED i2: Tests for {@link SeekableInMemoryByteChannel}, a {@link SeekableByteChannel} backed by an in-memory byte array.
ADDED i3: Reading into a buffer larger than the channel's contents returns only the available bytes (the channel size), leaving the rest of the buffer unfilled.
ADDED i4: 2402 capacity - 2245 bytes read = 157 bytes still free in the buffer.
ADDED i5: Writing a full buffer consumes every byte of the buffer and reports the number of bytes written.
ADDED i6: The source buffer is now fully drained: position advanced to its limit.
ADDED i7: Writing while the position exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE is rejected with an IOException.
ADDED i8: Integer.MAX_VALUE + 4
ADDED i10: Both {@code position} and {@code truncate} return a still-open channel and can be chained.
ADDED i11: Truncating returns the same channel instance (a fluent self-reference).
ADDED i12: Truncating to a negative size is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i14: Writing to a zero-capacity channel still succeeds: the backing buffer grows to accommodate all the data.
ADDED i15: After truncating an empty channel to zero, a write still appends all bytes and advances the source buffer's position.
ADDED i16: Reading from a channel truncated to zero (no data available) returns -1.
ADDED i17: Reading while the position is beyond Integer.MAX_VALUE returns -1 (end of stream) rather than throwing.
ADDED i18: Integer.MAX_VALUE + 4
ADDED i19: Reading into a buffer smaller than the channel's contents fills the whole buffer and reports the buffer's capacity as the byte count.
ADDED i20: Setting a negative position is rejected with an IllegalArgumentException.
ADDED i22: The default constructor allocates the default 8192-byte backing array.
ADDED i23: A channel constructed with size zero reports a size of zero.
ADDED i24: Reading after the channel is closed throws ClosedChannelException.
ADDED i26: A freshly created channel starts at position zero.
